summary.intent: Execute Phase 60 ('IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout') of the CipherBox project using the GSD wave-based parallel execution workflow, implementing strict fail-closed IPNS verification across Rust and TypeScript layers.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (plans 60-01, 60-02, 60-03) completed successfully with all 251 sdk-core tests passing. Wave 2 began with plan 60-04 dispatched to a subagent; transcript ends mid-execution.

repo: Phase 60 has 8 plans across 4 waves; Wave 4 (60-08) is non-autonomous and requires a human-action checkpoint for staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test.

The GSD worktree isolation mode ('isolation=worktree') is unreliable for merge-back in this harness — sequential subagents on the feature branch is the safer execution model for crypto-critical phases.
60-01 removed VerifyError::Legacy variant (D-04) and folded all 9 FUSE caller arms as a compile necessity, pulling work that was nominally scoped to 60-04.
60-02 unified all 9 first-publish IPNS producers to seq=1 (D-02); Windows WinFSP site is CI-gated and cannot be locally verified.

60-03 deleted the legacy else fall-through in resolveIpnsRecord (D-05), added resolve-side EOL/expiry enforcement via CBOR Validity parsing (D-07 TS path), and was forced to fix a stale vault.test.ts expectation (0n→1n) left by 60-02.
No project-specific executor skills payload exists for this project (gsd-tools query returned empty).
No submodules present — all plans use worktree isolation config but sequential mode was chosen instead.
sdk-core has 251 tests total, 34 of which are ipns-specific; these are the primary integration gate between Wave 1 plans.

code.finding: Previously referenced VerifyError::Legacy; executor folded this arm to VerifyError::Invalid as part of 60-01. The mid-edit compiler snapshot showing E0599 was stale — final state is clean.
Slated for deletion in 60-04 (now-empty re-export file after 60-01 relocated the verify chokepoint to crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs).
New home for the verified-IPNS-resolve implementation after 60-01 relocation; shared by sdk, fuse, and desktop.

workflow: Mid-execution compiler errors from subagent diagnostics can be stale snapshots taken mid-edit; always run an authoritative cargo check on the final tree before treating them as real failures.
When a subagent is forced to fold caller arms as a compile necessity (not just as declared scope), it can pull work from a later plan — requires cross-wave scope accounting.
The GSD sequential executor model (no worktree isolation) is preferred over parallel worktree agents when plans have tight compile-time coupling or when the phase is high-risk (crypto correctness).
Post-wave build/test gates should cover cross-plan integration points explicitly (e.g., 60-01↔60-02 in fuse/metadata.rs, 60-02↔60-03 in sdk-core) rather than only per-plan checks.

friction: Worktree isolation merge-back is not reliably supported by the harness, forcing a fallback to sequential execution and sacrificing parallelism for correctness.

Subagent diagnostic output included a stale E0599 compile error (VerifyError::Legacy) that required manual verification via grep and cargo check before continuing — false alarm cost investigation time.
60-02 left a stale vault.test.ts expectation (0n→1n) that 60-03 had to discover and fix, indicating cross-plan test coupling that wasn't captured in the dependency graph.
Executor skills payload is empty — no project-specific context is available to subagents beyond what the orchestrator embeds in the prompt.
